description: A taxpayer receives an official notice after filing and needs to decode the stated issue, identify which records are relevant, and organize a response packet without losing the timeline of the original return.

user_profile.persona: 37-year-old small business employee with limited experience handling tax correspondence
user_profile.context: The notice sounds serious, but it is not yet clear whether the issue is a typo, missing record, or real discrepancy
user_profile.communication_style: Careful and exact, wants the notice translated into plain next steps

fact_sheet.fact: The taxpayer's name is Elias Vance.
Elias Vance is 37 years old.
Elias Vance is employed as a logistics coordinator at 'Crimson Cartography Supplies'.
The tax return in question is for the 2023 tax year.
The original 2023 tax return was electronically filed on April 11, 2024.
The tax preparation software used for the filing was 'SwiftTax Pro'.
The e-filing confirmation number for the return is ST2024-ELEC-98B3-C4D7.
The Adjusted Gross Income (AGI) reported on the original Form 1040 was $68,550.
The notice was issued by the 'Federal Revenue Service' (FRS).
The official notice number is FRS-CP2000.
The notice is dated June 10, 2024.
The deadline to respond to the notice is July 10, 2024.
The title of the notice is 'Proposed Changes to Your 2023 Form 1040'.
The FRS internal case ID assigned to this issue is 8801-45-23-VANCE-E.
The notice claims there is unreported income from a Form 1099-MISC.
The payer listed on the unreported Form 1099-MISC is 'Blue Peak Freelance Collective'.
The amount of unreported income cited by the FRS is $4,200.
The proposed additional tax due based on the discrepancy is $924.
The FRS has proposed a penalty of $46.20 for substantial understatement of tax.
Elias needs to locate his copy of the Form 1099-MISC received from 'Blue Peak Freelance Collective' for the 2023 tax year.
To verify the income, Elias needs to gather his bank statements for his primary checking account (ending in -5678) covering the period from January 1, 2023 to December 31, 2023.
A signed written statement explaining why the income was not reported must be included in the response packet.
Elias must include a copy of the original Form 1040 he filed on April 11, 2024.
To agree with the changes, Elias must sign and return the enclosed FRS Form 4549, 'Income Tax Examination Changes'.
All correspondence must be mailed to: Federal Revenue Service, Notice Response Unit 5, P.O. Box 7123, Ogden, UT 84201.
The recommended method for sending the response packet is via Certified Mail with Return Receipt to ensure proof of delivery.
The FRS helpline for this notice is 1-800-555-0219, available Monday through Friday from 7 AM to 7 PM Central Time.
Elias can consult his tax preparer, Maria Chen at 'Chen Accounting Services', at phone number 555-890-1234 for professional advice.
Elias stores his digital tax records in a folder named 'Tax_Records_2023' on his personal laptop's encrypted hard drive.
The specific discrepancy in the notice is that FRS says Elias's original 2023 return omitted a Form 1099-MISC from Blue Peak Freelance Collective reporting $4,200 of income.
The complete response packet described by the notice materials includes the 1099-MISC copy, the supporting bank statements, a signed written statement, and a copy of the original Form 1040.

user_needs.description: What is the notice number and title, and which agency sent it?
What is the deadline to respond to this notice?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: After identifying a notice, the user's immediate next concern is the deadline for action.

user_needs.description: What specific discrepancy does the FRS say exists on my 2023 return?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Cross-group: Once the user understands the notice's identity and deadline, the next logical step is to understand the core problem.

user_needs.description: What is the name of the payer and the amount of unreported income cited in the notice?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: After learning the issue is unreported income, the user will want the specific details of that income.

user_needs.description: How much additional tax and penalty does the FRS say I owe?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Cross-group: After understanding the source and amount of the discrepancy, the user will want to know the financial consequences.

user_needs.description: What specific documents, like tax forms and bank statements, do I need to find to address this issue?
What other items must be included in the full response packet besides the core evidence documents?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: After identifying the primary evidence, a careful user will want to know about all other required components for the response packet.

user_needs.description: What is the mailing address for the response packet and what is the recommended sending method?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Cross-group: Once the user knows what documents to assemble, the next step is to figure out where and how to send the completed packet.

user_needs.description: Is there a professional tax preparer I can contact for advice on this matter?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Cross-group: Seeing the specific amount of tax and penalty owed (the financial impact) can trigger the user to seek professional help.

user_needs.description: What is the FRS internal case ID assigned to my issue?
